prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 — Summary

We stand for Scotland: for Independence, for completing the powers of the Scottish Parliament, and for putting Scotland first at Westminster. Every SNP MP is a vote for Independence, for more powers now, and for defending Scotland from Westminster’s failures. A majority of SNP MPs will trigger a referendum on Independence.

Our contract with the people
- Drive Scotland to Independence via a democratic referendum.
- Deliver the best deal for Scotland.
- Protect Scotland from harmful Westminster decisions.

Our Independence vision
- A just, caring, enterprising Scotland with a modern, written constitution, inclusive citizenship, PR at all levels, and the Queen retained as Head of State by consent.
- Use Scotland’s wealth for Scotland: create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations using oil revenues, and a Scottish Trust for Public Investment (STPI) to replace costly PFI/PPP and upgrade infrastructure.

Key policies
- Education: abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants; establish an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 classes to 18; end damaging league tables; refurbish schools via STPI; strengthen Gaelic medium education, inclusion, anti-racism, rural schools, and ICT.
- Jobs & enterprise: invest in transport, broadband, reskilling; reform development agencies; elevate tourism marketing and access; devolve and refocus New Deal; raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; guarantee union rights.
- Environment: lead on sustainability; climate risk strategy; renewables 12% of energy by 2010 (25% electricity); no new nuclear; decommission Dounreay; resource efficiency; fair water charging; oppose backdoor privatisation.
- Health: National Health Care Commission; prevention (free fruit in schools; healthier school meals); end postcode treatment with binding HTBS decisions; free dental check-ups; fairer prescription charges; invest via STPI; clean hospitals; +1,500 nurses; halve inpatient waiting times; free personal care for the elderly.
- Europe: Scotland in a confederal EU with stronger subsidiarity; Euro by consent when conditions are right; far greater influence with Independence.
- Defence: remove Trident; oppose US missile defence; phase withdrawal from NATO’s nuclear structures; form a professional Scottish Defence Force; fair share of defence spending while in the UK.
- International & aid: business-focused External Affairs Offices; meet UN aid targets; cancel Third World debt; untie aid.
- Culture, sport, languages: reform arts funding; national theatre; Scottish Lottery for good causes; community sport and football academies; secure status for Gaelic; promote Scots.
- Social justice: national anti-poverty strategy; humane, fast and fair asylum; empower voluntary sector; tackle homelessness.
- Housing: UK to assume historic housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via STPI; tenants first; oppose wholesale stock transfer.
- Equality & disability: devolve equalities powers; strengthen DDA; disability equality indicator.
- Crime & drugs: +1,000 police; drugs courts; parental compensation orders; lifelong restriction for high-risk sex offenders; retain justice funds in Scotland.
- Tax: no overall tax rise without mandate; comprehensive tax review; immediate 10p/gal fuel duty cut funded by a 5p income tax band over £100k.
- Local government: fair long-term funding; PR (STV); review finance incl. local income tax.
- Rural, agriculture, fisheries: cut fuel duty; small business relief; ICT and transport; protect key rural services; fair EU playing field; diversify and promote quality produce; reform CFP with zonal management; compensated tie-ups; salmon farming inquiry; empower SEPA; community land rights.
- Pensions & social security: restore earnings link; spread winter fuel payments; simplify benefits with a single agency; improve take-up; fairer support for disabled, carers, and young people.
- Transport: fair UK share; RTAs; public stake in Railtrack; reopen lines; electrify priorities; concessionary travel; targeted road upgrades; lower ferry fares/RET pilots; more direct flights; abolish Skye Bridge tolls.
